title: Usage frequency predicts lexicalization across languages
title_zh: 使用频率预测语言间的词汇化
abstract: Languages are more likely to have lexical items for some concepts (such as CHILD and SUN) than others (such as PARENT and WEATHER). Here we present a large-scale quantitative analysis of factors that predict lexicalization across languages, and test in particular the hypothesis that usage frequency predicts lexicalization. We consider 854 concepts and demonstrate that average usage frequency across 46 languages from the Language Documentation Reference Corpus is a relatively good predictor of the typological prevalence of lexicalization across the 41 languages in the World Loanword Database (β = 0.25; 95% confidence interval, (0.16, 0.33)) and across 262 languages from the Intercontinental Dictionary Series (β = 0.30; 95% confidence interval, (0.23, 0.38)). This finding implies that cross-linguistic regularities in lexicalization can be attributed in part to shared usage patterns across cultures. Why do almost all human languages have a word for ‘sun’, but fewer have a word for ‘weather’? Khishigsuren et al. find that the usefulness of a concept in communication predicts how often it appears in vocabularies across languages.
abstract_zh: 语言更有可能对某些概念（例如“CHILD”和“SUN”）设有词汇条目，而非其他概念（例如“PARENT”和“WEATHER”）。本文提出了一项大规模定量分析，以研究预测语言间词汇化的因素，并特别检验了使用频率预测词汇化的假设。我们考察了854个概念，并发现，来自语言文献参考语料库（Language Documentation Reference Corpus）中46种语言的平均使用频率，能够较好地预测世界借词数据库（World Loanword Database）中41种语言词汇化的类型学普遍性（β = 0.25；95%置信区间为0.16至0.33），以及大陆词典系列（Intercontinental Dictionary Series）中262种语言词汇化的普遍性（β = 0.30；95%置信区间为0.23至0.38）。这一发现表明，跨语言词汇化的规律性部分可归因于文化间共享的使用模式。为什么几乎所有人类语言都有表示“太阳”的词，而只有少数语言有表示“天气”的词？Khishigsuren 等人发现，概念在交流中的实用性预测了其在各语言词汇中出现的频率。
